A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CPO study. The main text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–J support reliable comparison, including matching content moved between the appendices and main text.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations on CUB, AwA2 and CelebA, including concept prediction, classification, interventions, noise robustness and streaming updates.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in its main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The CPO objective in Equation 5, policy-sampled negative concepts, Gumbel-Softmax sampling and prior-based streaming updates remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Datasets and evaluated scenarios are retained. The confidence-based CUB noise experiment in v2 Section 5.3 was already evaluated in v1 Appendix H.2; the cropping and occlusion examples also existed in Appendix G.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same BCE-trained CBMs/CEMs, joint and sequential ProbCBMs, and CoopCBM where previously included. The relocated confidence-noise table retains the same four model rows.

E3.justification: Splits, metrics, training settings, intervention procedures, noise probabilities and streaming partitions are unchanged. v2 Section 5.3 repeats the confidence-to-noise mapping previously documented in v1 Appendix H.2.

E4.justification: The gradient, noise-sensitivity, streaming-initialization and uncertainty analyses are retained. v2 Figure 3 redisplays the white-underparts example from v1 Figure 13, while the confidence-noise analysis moves into the main text.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same reporting through ± table entries and plotted error bars or bands. No run-count, seed, interval-estimation or statistical-testing information is added.

E6.justification: Matched tables and plots retain their results. For example, confidence-noised CUB CBM-CPO remains at 0.793±0.002 task accuracy and 0.913±0.000 concept AUC in v1 Table 3 and v2 Table 2. The new Figure 3 repeats existing example values.

T1.justification: Sections 3–4 and Appendices C and E retain the same mathematical definitions, assumptions, propositions, theorem and derivations. The added uncertainty explanation introduces no new formal result.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution framing and conclusion retain the same claims about concept posteriors, noise robustness, interventions and streaming learning without additional model parameters.

C2.justification: The added Section 4.3 discussion restates Appendix G's interpretation of uncertainty under cropping and occlusion. Existing qualifications, including modest aggregate uncertainty differences between CPO and BCE, remain in that appendix.

D1.justification: Implementation, preprocessing, hyperparameter, hardware, timing and repository disclosures are retained. v2's statement that CPO and BCE tune the same number of hyperparameters summarizes already documented settings.

R1.justification: The bibliography and related-work positioning are unchanged. The additional Kim et al. (2023) citation accompanying the uncertainty example refers to an already discussed work.

P1.justification: v2 expands Section 4.3's explanation, moves Appendix H.2 into Section 5.3 with a rewritten introduction, simplifies Appendix H's structure, and adds acknowledgments and publication metadata. Most prose and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figure 3 by isolating and relabeling an existing appendix example, moves the confidence-noise table into the main text, and resizes or repositions displays. The final appendices are laid out more compactly; existing visual evidence is retained.

improvement.justification: v2 makes existing evidence easier to find and understand: Section 5.3 brings confidence-based noise evaluation into the main narrative, while Figure 3 and the expanded Section 4.3 connect the posterior discussion to a concrete occlusion example. These provide modest exposition benefits; the scientific evidence, theory and reproducibility information remain unchanged.
